memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Love the Lord your God and keep his requirements, his decrees, his laws and his commands always. Remember today that your children were not the ones who saw and experienced the discipline of the Lord your God: his majesty, his mighty hand, his outstretched arm; the signs he performed and the things he did in the heart of Egypt, both to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his whole country. - Deut 11:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses joins two things that belong together: "Love the Lord your God and keep his requirements." Love and obedience are not opposites, nor are they separate. Real love for God naturally expresses itself in doing what He asks. Moses then urges the people to remember what God had done — His mighty acts in Egypt, His majesty, His powerful deliverance. Love grows out of remembering. When we recall who God is and what He has done, our hearts are drawn to love and follow Him.

We sometimes imagine that love is only a feeling, while obedience is a cold duty. But Scripture ties them together beautifully. To love God is to trust Him enough to follow His ways; to obey Him is one of the truest expressions of love. When a child truly loves and trusts a good parent, obedience flows naturally, not grudgingly. So it is with our heavenly Father.

Jesus said it plainly: "If you love me, keep my commands" (John 14:15). Notice the order — love comes first, and obedience flows from it. This is not legalism, where we obey to earn love. It is the response of a heart that has already been loved and rescued. And the key to it all, as Moses shows, is remembering. When our love grows cold, the remedy is to return to what God has done — supremely the cross of Christ — and let that memory rekindle our love. Remember His mighty acts today, and let your love overflow into glad obedience.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I see love for God and obedience as connected, or as opposites?
- How does remembering what God has done stir my love for Him?
- When my love grows cold, do I return to remembering His mighty acts?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to love You truly, and let that love overflow into glad obedience. When my heart grows cold, draw me back to remember all You have done, especially the cross of Christ, and rekindle my love for You. Amen.
